relevant_claims.title: Retain nine BIT arrival price floors with arbitrary rational relay charts
relevant_claims.body:
**The nine original rank-seven BIT arrivals into chart 0 retain minimum price `7^t` even with arbitrary new rational relay charts**, for `0<t<=1`. New charts have zero initial scratch and no new source information; original earlier stock, retention and local XOR are free, and every nested transfer is charged. This closes the new-chart opening in [PR #7750](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7750) for these nine deadlines. **No new kappa**, whole-word relay theorem or additive lower bound for a shared multi-output network is claimed.

Read the [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9fda92fea5ed634471df177c27f1f74eeea5a166/research/bit-rational-relay-price-floor/PROOF.md), [complete pair certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9fda92fea5ed634471df177c27f1f74eeea5a166/research/bit-rational-relay-price-floor/RESULT.json), [verifier](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9fda92fea5ed634471df177c27f1f74eeea5a166/research/bit-rational-relay-price-floor/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9fda92fea5ed634471df177c27f1f74eeea5a166/research/bit-rational-relay-price-floor/SOURCE-PINS.json) and [credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9fda92fea5ed634471df177c27f1f74eeea5a166/research/bit-rational-relay-price-floor/CREDITS.md).

The proposed dimension-three hub cannot gather the required original dimension-four stocks: among all **2,415 distinct pairs**, intersections have dimension zero or two, never three. More generally, subspace distance makes any tree joining chart 0 to three original dimension-four charts cost at least eight, even through arbitrary new subspaces. A cheaper network has total rank at most six, so its relevant component contains at most two such stocks. Its support is at most **42**, or at most **35** when it reaches an original dimension-six stock. Every target-coset representative has weight at least **48**.

```text
delta(A,B) = dim(A)+dim(B)-2 dim(A intersect B)
three original four-spaces plus zero: tree cost >= 8
cheaper target network: rank sum <= 6, support <= 42 < 48
```

| Evidence | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| Complete four-space geometry | 70 charts, 2,415 pairs: 1,155 intersections of dimension zero and 1,260 of dimension two |
| Separate rank paths | Integer elimination and rank modulo the verified prime 1,000,003 agree on every pair |
| Retained source replay | All stock supports, 511 target cosets, paid-row/source attainments and the complete nested-chain bound |
| Scope control | A changed coordinate geometry really admits the proposed rank-six star; its common three-space fails the actual source pair premise |
| Rejection controls | A duplicate pair and all three changed-geometry source pairs fail the required distance floor |

Python 3.12, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-rational-relay-price-floor
```

Both registered normal and optimized commands print:

```text
PASS_BIT_RATIONAL_RELAY_PRICE_FLOOR 2415 pairs; support<=42<48
```

Normal/optimized registered replay, committed bytes/source history/modes, export and sealed read-only Git-free serial replay pass. Hosted CI is pending; it is not scientific evidence yet. The general new-chart conclusion follows from the metric and information-component proof, not a finite sampling of possible rational charts.

Ali Romman supplied the [fixed-chart proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/PROOF.md), [chain certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/RESULT.json) and [PR #7741](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7741)'s quotient/coset result. Nick Petalas supplied [PR #7739](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7739)'s original reduction and nine exceptions. [PR #7723](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7723) supplied the fixed-library model; Jerry Chen supplied the selected [PR #7001](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7001) caller. The [retained credit file](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/CREDITS.md) preserves zxv, DreamingOfClouds, Cinna Davis and earlier native/root attribution. All source bytes and notices remain intact.

Each conclusion concerns one original target and its fixed original earlier stock. The nine minima cannot be summed for a jointly changed network that creates shared earlier information. The other 5,733 arrivals, new source promises, changed rows/deadlines and uncharged cross-chart operations need separate analysis. No physical construction for free storage or new-chart access is supplied. All five framework assumptions and the selected frontier remain unchanged. The selected cold replay, unrelated historical suites, Lean, Docker and physical relay execution were not run.

relevant_claims.body:

This permits new intermediate forms, branching, merging, cycles and cancellation. It extends [PR #7741](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7741)'s direct-bundle result at these nine deadlines. **No new kappa** or relay guarantee at the other 5,733 arrivals is claimed.

Read the [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/PROOF.md), [tree/path receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/RESULT.json), [verifier](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/verify.py), [exact source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/SOURCE-PINS.json) and [credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/CREDITS.md).

Every improving network must have total integer rank at most six. Its relevant chart component has a spanning tree within that budget. If a dimension-six chart occurs, the whole tree is a strictly increasing nested chain from zero to six. Otherwise its dimensions are 0, 1, 2 and 4. These cases bound the support of every form available to the receiver, even after new relay combinations.

| Complete necessary bound | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Low-dimensional trees: support at most 37 | Exact rooted-tree recurrence with arbitrary branching; an independent coarse cut bound also gives 42<48 |
| Chains reaching dimension six: support at most 35 | All 37,872 chains; exact source support unions |
| Separate path census | Forward and reverse constructions agree on all 40,667 increasing paths |
| Required arrivals: distance at least 48 | All 511 target-coset vectors in the unchanged predecessor certificate |
| Attained old price | The original source and nested rank-seven transfer remain feasible |

Thus every cheaper network has projected nonroot support at most **37**, while every required target representative has weight at least **48**. The old direct-only cap of 30 does fail on an actual relay chain; the new result charges and covers that changed information flow. The 37 bound is an upper bound for actual stock, not a claimed exact communication capacity.

relevant_claims.title: Prove the exact four-qubit Clifford Gram rank at width nine
relevant_claims.body:
## Summary

Scoped proof produced by Nick Petalas. The full projective four-qubit Gaussian-dyadic Clifford tensor Gram at width nine has rank **10,107,260,791,808** out of **12,128,668,876,800**. Its nullity is **2,021,408,084,992**, so the pointwise independence threshold satisfies **T(4) ≥ 10**.

This answers the first character calculation proposed in alephnan's [PR #6714](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6714). The proof identifies the quotient character with the action on ordered four-tuples of binary symplectic vectors and computes the occupied Clifford matrix blocks. It takes the published ordinary S8(2) character table as input. Credit also goes to aliromman [#5526](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5526) for the pointwise framework and to the ATLAS and Thomas Breuer's CTblLib for the table.

## Evidence

The exact calculation finds 61 present and 20 missing quotient irreducibles. A separate orbit calculation checks all nine moments of the fixed-dimension histogram. Two controls reject a changed character sum and an incorrect bin assignment. The published table archive reproduced the complete integer projection locally.

Run from the repository root with CPython 3.12.15.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-four-qubit-width-nine
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/clifford-four-qubit-width-nine --check-source-history
python3.12 -B -W error research/clifford-four-qubit-width-nine/verify.py
```

To rederive the integer projection from the published source:

```sh
scratch_dir=$(mktemp -d)
curl -fsSL 'https://www.math.rwth-aachen.de/~Thomas.Breuer/ctbllib/ctbllib-1.3.11.tar.gz' \
  -o "$scratch_dir/ctbllib-1.3.11.tar.gz"
python3.12 -B -W error research/clifford-four-qubit-width-nine/verify.py \
  --ctbllib-archive "$scratch_dir/ctbllib-1.3.11.tar.gz"
```

## Limitations

The claim concerns exact operators at width nine. Width-ten independence, formal proof-kernel review, physical caller integration, and recursive cost accounting remain open. The selected multiplication theorem and its premises lie outside the claim.

## Open next questions

- Decide width-ten independence. Begin with the two quadratic-form stabilizers and test whether the twenty missing odd-sector rows can support a missing even-sector block under tensor reciprocity.

## Related open work

The overlap search found no open PR computing the four-qubit width-nine Gram rank or nullity.

## CI notes

This PR carries the shared CI-doc and replay-gap sync used by other open PRs. [Passing CI on PR #7654](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44200077426)

The current-status suite reproduced the stale CI section before the sync and passed all six tests after it. The historical replay-gap package and the Clifford rank package both passed locally on CPython 3.12.15.

All three hosted jobs passed at `ff12ca358d601a21cd4b1f016b8a3a969ac44016`. They covered planning, the Clifford rank package, and the historical replay-gap package. [Registered research packages run](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44400354668)

relevant_claims.title: Prove an all-bundle direct-delivery price floor for the selected BIT word
relevant_claims.body:
**Every original paid BIT arrival retains its minimum price under arbitrary finite bundles of direct nested deliveries from its fixed, strictly earlier chart libraries.** This closes the nine higher-arity exceptions left by [PR #7739](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7739). The theorem covers both orientations, all 659 independent inputs, free retention and destination XOR, and every tariff `rank^t` for `0<t<=1`. The original single delivery attains the floor. **No new kappa** follows; the compatible paid-moment gain within this contract is at most zero.

Read the [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/33817d65c801232f1e07355f43ec6040a41e7c7e/research/bit-all-bundle-price-floor/PROOF.md), [full support/coset certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/33817d65c801232f1e07355f43ec6040a41e7c7e/research/bit-all-bundle-price-floor/RESULT.json), [verifier](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/33817d65c801232f1e07355f43ec6040a41e7c7e/research/bit-all-bundle-price-floor/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/33817d65c801232f1e07355f43ec6040a41e7c7e/research/bit-all-bundle-price-floor/SOURCE-PINS.json) and [credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/33817d65c801232f1e07355f43ec6040a41e7c7e/research/bit-all-bundle-price-floor/CREDITS.md).

The predecessor already excludes 5,733 of 5,742 arrivals by the sum of all lower-rank donor spaces. The remaining nine are rank-seven arrivals into chart 0. A strictly cheaper bundle must have total rank at most six. In one fixed 135-dimensional quotient, the largest donor support unions at ranks 1, 2, 4 and 6 have sizes 1, 2, 17 and 30. Thus every affordable bundle, of any arity, has support at most 30. The complete target cosets have minimum weights **56, 58, 52, 50, 51, 50, 50, 48, 48**. Each exceeds 30.

Keeping the initial quotient is essential: the later free destination rows remain an explicit span of dimension at most eight. This reduces the whole higher-arity question to **511 exact coset vectors**, without enumerating arbitrary donor subsets. It proves an obstruction in this model, not a failed finite search.

| Evidence | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| New support certificate | All 514 eligible donors; exact support masks, ranks and image dimensions |
| New target distances | All 511 coset vectors, full weight histograms and minimum witnesses |
| Causal stability | 4,112 donor-library equality checks across later deadlines |
| Separate row representation | Coordinate sets agree with the retained packed interpreter on all 5,742 paid rows |
| Attainment | Every original source contains its required row at the old deadline; all original pairs are nested |
| Replayed dependency | The predecessor's 5,733 full-span exclusions, 4,626 singleton checks and 478,764 pair checks |
| Controls | Four false support caps, nine current-arrival deadline leaks, strict budget and binary addition |

The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence. The source rational geometry and full-donor reduction are shared code. Separate row reconstruction is not independent human or formal-kernel acceptance.

Credit Nick Petalas for the [full-donor reduction and two-delivery proof](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7e44f44b8078b3788256772533890fbf85503a0c/research/bit-causal-multi-delivery/README.md) and [checker](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7e44f44b8078b3788256772533890fbf85503a0c/research/bit-causal-multi-delivery/verify.py). Ali Romman's [PR #7723](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7723) supplied the [fixed-library model](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a4fd22c08058c0fef830306b2d46e4a51f091939/research/bit-causal-delivery-rank-obstruction/PROOF.md). Jerry Chen supplied the selected [PR #7001](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7001) caller; its [notice](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57/research/paired-query-only-bit/NOTICE) credits zxv and the retained native authors, DreamingOfClouds for the chain-root caller, and the earlier root lineage. relevant_claims.title: Prove the global ceiling for simultaneous helper restrictions on the selected BIT word
relevant_claims.body:
**No simultaneous choice of block-local linear helper restrictions improves the selected BIT caller’s raw crossing.** Over all 437 helpers in its nine boundary groups, in either word orientation, the supremum of price savings with a strictly positive complete margin lies between **0.0038525393934 and 0.0038525393935**. PR7001 already reported this interval for the original caller. This contribution proves its optimality over the entire specified family. At the project’s 0.01 target, even the best signed margin is strictly between **−2355.302 and −2355.301**. The selected conditional multiplication saving is **0.00363005817**. [Proof, including the full-interval ceiling](https://github.com/alephnan/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f2efcb571858c18f5f0392379c7d08f0675d0eaa/research/bit-simultaneous-helper-relations/PROOF.md) · [Exact certificate](https://github.com/alephnan/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f2efcb571858c18f5f0392379c7d08f0675d0eaa/research/bit-simultaneous-helper-relations/RESULT.json) · [Selected application review](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57/docs/research/pr-intake-evidence/pr7000-application/PROOF-REVIEW.md)

At price $r^t$, for $\log_2(5/3)\le t\le1$, the largest change in the complete 36-call margin is exactly

$$
36\max\{0,\ 1+4^t-6^t\}.
$$

Setting helper 341 to zero attains the second branch. It removes one rank-one and one rank-four payment per invocation and surrenders one rank-six target. An edit first improves the old margin when the price-saving parameter $1-t$ exceeds 0.2517782975220009…. The complete bill is already negative there. The proof separately bounds the entire remaining range, including this apparent opportunity.

**Why the one-group exclusions do not add automatically.** The forward bank at chart 50, clock 19881, contains $x_{331}+x_{332}+x_{333}$. The equations $x_{331}=0$ and $x_{332}+x_{333}=0$ belong to different groups. Together they make the bank reconstructible, while either equation alone still requires payment. The proof accounts for such interactions with chronological rank increments, projects the mixed final spaces onto the 410-dimensional group, and classifies the optimizing tuples. [Predecessor’s one-group theorem](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7722) · [Receiver and pivot verifier](https://github.com/alephnan/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f2efcb571858c18f5f0392379c7d08f0675d0eaa/research/bit-simultaneous-helper-relations/flags.py)

**Reproduction.** From the repository root, CPython 3.12 and its standard library suffice.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-simultaneous-helper-relations
```

Both registered checks pass. One recomputes all 636 rational frames, 2,374 directed paid chart pairs and 3,530 bank prefixes per orientation. The other solves the column nullspaces from a separate word interpreter, checks all 820 large-block coordinate prices in order, and directly enumerates 64,882 small-block subspaces across both orientations. The Windows CPython 3.12.2 replay, Linux CPython 3.14.7 replay, PR7001’s original BIT application, committed-byte/source-history preflight and a Git-free export replay passed. [Independent implementation](https://github.com/alephnan/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f2efcb571858c18f5f0392379c7d08f0675d0eaa/research/bit-simultaneous-helper-relations/crosscheck.py) · [Whole-invoice arithmetic](https://github.com/alephnan/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f2efcb571858c18f5f0392379c7d08f0675d0eaa/research/bit-simultaneous-helper-relations/invoice_bound.py) · [Replay guide](https://github.com/alephnan/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f2efcb571858c18f5f0392379c7d08f0675d0eaa/research/bit-simultaneous-helper-relations/README.md)

The construction grants all historical same-chart receiver banks and scalar XOR for free. Boundary equations are block-local, the paid forms and routes are fixed, and the two directions are analyzed separately. A changed causal delivery after a restriction is an open next step. relevant_claims.title: Execute the half-sum CLEAR on fixed tapes with a complete scan bill
relevant_claims.body:
This gives a fixed-tape execution and complete local scan bill for the exact half-sum CLEAR circuit in [PR #7721](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7721). At width 1076, the emitted program uses **589,841 unit data instructions and 11,206,982 interpreter steps**. It preserves all donors, implements the target XOR and invalid flag, restores every work cell and temporary bit, and returns all 26 heads. **No new kappa is claimed.**

Read the [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/PROOF.md), [receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/RESULT.json), [emitted binary program](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/PROGRAM-1076.bits.gz), [compiler and tape executor](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/tape.py), [checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/SOURCE-PINS.json) and [credit](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fae44c3ea2bc24e42f678365282f3737014fe9b3/research/half-sum-clear-tape/CREDITS.md). The [scoped claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19715135) answers the source's released tape-layout question.

The machine has 25 data tapes, one read-only program tape, a five-symbol alphabet, two temporary control bits and a width-independent finite decoder. Nine binary bits encode each unit movement, control read, target toggle or cell initialization/retirement. The program is read and returned in full. No random-access gate lookup is assumed during execution.

| Resource at width 1076 | Exact count |
| --- | ---: |
| Data bit cells | 24,788 |
| Work bit cells, included above | 15,103 |
| Peak data markers | 50 |
| Marked program cells | 5,308,571 |
| Unit data instructions | 589,841 |
| Interpreter steps | 11,206,982 |

For every positive width, the proof gives `L<=1222w+2952` instructions and `19L+3<=23218w+56091` interpreter steps. It charges ripple access, flags, output copy, reverse execution, initialization, retirement and all head returns. This bound follows from the literal column loops; it is not fitted to measured values. Work cells start blank and return blank. The original external markers and program remain unchanged.

The entrance supplies the marked width-dependent program, input blocks, origins and reserved blank regions. **Uniform physical program generation/loading and enclosing stock/reset services remain open.** This is a classical multi-tape execution model; transition-level reversible control is not claimed. The complete external XOR map is reversible and its local workspace is restored. No selected owned-erasure or precision-tape assumption is discharged.

Base: `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. The six scientific files from PR #7721, published head `8f6279527c4362e2638737c90fa18c3cfec724fa`, are retained unchanged. Its [source proof and credit](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/8f6279527c4362e2638737c90fa18c3cfec724fa/research/half-sum-clear-circuit/README.md) establish the all-width arithmetic map. Its source verifier is rerun. The native event88937 identification is inherited from [PR #7687](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7687) and its [exact interface](https://github.com/SYLforge/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e5ba67dfd6237a1a3acf4d67098d3242adee8229/research/clean-rational-clear-witness/README.md); that whole native check was not rerun. [PR #3233](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3233) prices a different pooled field ADD; no code or constant is reused from it.

Run with CPython 3.12 and its standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/half-sum-clear-tape
```

Each registered command prints the retained source result, then:

```text
PASS_HALF_SUM_CLEAR_FIXED_TAPE {'1': 1024, '2': 65536, '1076': 32} 11206982
```

Normal and optimized replay pass. The tape checker executes all 1,024 width-one combinations, all 65,536 width-two donor tuples with varied output bits, and the 32 published width-1076 fixtures. It checks every tape cell and head against direct integer arithmetic. Five damaged streams are rejected. An endpoint-preserving extra right/left detour costs exactly 38 additional steps. Source bytes, committed history/modes, package export, sealed read-only Git-free replay, public links and rendered publication readback pass. Hosted CI did not certify this package. The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44372462678/job/135042649052) failed in the shared `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the base guide names frontier6030 while the selected record requires `make frontier7000-verify`. The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence.

Program preparation, global stock/reset, rounded producer reachability and native/caller admission remain explicit obligations. Full predecessor suites, selected cold replay, Lean and Docker were not run. This is source-aware author checking, not blind, independent human or formal acceptance. No selected-frontier or other workstream change is included.

relevant_claims.body:
This construction gives **conditional κ ≥ 0.00378751509478**. Its certified lower endpoint exceeds the upper endpoint of PR #7717 by **0.00002437823416 (0.64782%)**. That gain is **15.24% larger** than the preceding gain of 0.00002115478655 reported in PR #7713. The new raw crossing lies in **[0.00378751509486, 0.00378751509487]**. [Construction proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/3ba9094c54b61f424d2f98cd2c6ca64c01baf9d3/research/p104-interleaved-helper-bases/PROOF.md) · [Complete application receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/3ba9094c54b61f424d2f98cd2c6ca64c01baf9d3/research/p104-interleaved-helper-bases/results/application.json)

Starting from the deposited PR #7713 circuit, 220 restrictions remove 230 paid returns. Twelve causal splits introduce fresh independent helpers. Fourteen paid pivots and nine hub reroutes complete the graph. Choosing different local equations at the same rank permits two independent splits at chart 288 and one at chart 306. Three counterexamples identify the exact input or output coefficients that fail under the alternate equations.
